questions.question: Development proceeds from head to toe. a) Cephalocaudal b) Proximodistal c) Body development d) None of these
questions.solution_html:
• Option A-LBW babies
  • Though the human being develops as a unified whole, each part of the body develops at
  • different rates. Basically there are two sequences in the rate of development.

  • first, then the trunk.

  • intelligence is associated with retardation in various aspects of development. (1 mark)

questions.question: The first immunisation to the infant a) Colostrum b) Hind milk c) Fore milk d) Transition milk
questions.solution_html:
•  Infectious Morbidity: Compared with breast fed infants,formula fed infants face higher
  • risk of infectious morbidity in the first year of life.These differences in health outcomes
  • can be explained by specific and innate immune factors present in human milk.
  •  Ear Infections(Otitis Media): Approximately,44 % of infants will have atleast 1
  • episode of otitis media in the first year of life,and the risk among formula-fed infants is
  • doubled compared with infants who are exclusively breast fed for more than 3 months.
  •  Lower Respiratory Tract Infection : Infants who were not breast fed face an increased
  • risk of hospitalization for lower respiratory tract infection in the first year of
  • life,compared with infants who were exclusively breast fed for more than 4 months.The
  • majority of respiratory hospitalizations for infants result from infection with RSV.
  •  Gastrointestinal Infections:Formulated infants face an increased risk of Gastroenteritis
  • and diarrhoea.
  •  Necrotizing Enterocolitis : Among pre-term infants,not being breast fed is associated
  • with an increased risk of Necrotizing Enterocolitis.
  •  Obesity and Metabolic Disease: Children who are formula-fed in infancy are more
  • likely to become obese or develop type 2 diabetes.Children formula-fed in infancy are 1
  • to 3 times likely to become obese as children who had ever been breast fed.Being
  • formula fed is associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes compared with being
  • breast fed.
  •  Neurodevelopment: Lower IQ scores are reported in formulated children compared with
  • breast fed children
  •  SIDS(Sudden Infant Death Syndrome): Formula feeding is associated with a higher
  • risk of infant mortality compared with breast feeding
  •  Infant Mortality : Formula feeding is associated with an increased risk of infant
  • mortality compared with breast feeding
  •  Asthma:There is a 1.7 fold risk of developing asthma among formula fed children with a
  • positive family history of asthma and a 1.4 fold risk of developing asthma among
  • formula fed children without a family history,compared with those who were breast fed
  • for 3 months or more
  •  Atopic Dermatitis : Infants with a family history of atopy who were exclusively
  • breastfed for less than 3 months have a 1.7 fold risk of atopic dermatitis compared with
  • infants who were exclusively breastfed.
  •  Type 1 Dermatitis : Less than 3 months of breast feeding has been associated with a 1.2
  • to 1.4 fold increased risk of developing type 1 diabetes compared with more than 3
  • months of breast feeding.
  •  Childhood Cancer:Several studies have examined associations between formula feeding
  • and childhood leukemia based on the hypothesis that immunoreactive factors in breast
  • milk may prevent viral infections implicated in the leukemia pathogenesis. (1 mark for
  • each point)

questions.question: List and explain the common health hazards of bottle feeding in infants.
questions.solution_html:
•  Infectious Morbidity: Compared with breast fed infants,formula fed infants face higher
  • risk of infectious morbidity in the first year of life.These differences in health outcomes
  • can be explained by specific and innate immune factors present in human milk.
  •  Ear Infections(Otitis Media): Approximately,44 % of infants will have atleast 1
  • episode of otitis media in the first year of life,and the risk among formula-fed infants is
  • doubled compared with infants who are exclusively breast fed for more than 3 months.
  •  Lower Respiratory Tract Infection : Infants who were not breast fed face an increased
  • risk of hospitalization for lower respiratory tract infection in the first year of
  • life,compared with infants who were exclusively breast fed for more than 4 months.The
  • majority of respiratory hospitalizations for infants result from infection with RSV.
  •  Gastrointestinal Infections:Formulated infants face an increased risk of Gastroenteritis
  • and diarrhoea.
  •  Necrotizing Enterocolitis : Among pre-term infants,not being breast fed is associated
  • with an increased risk of Necrotizing Enterocolitis.
  •  Obesity and Metabolic Disease: Children who are formula-fed in infancy are more
  • likely to become obese or develop type 2 diabetes.Children formula-fed in infancy are 1
  • to 3 times likely to become obese as children who had ever been breast fed.Being
  • formula fed is associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes compared with being
  • breast fed.
  •  Neurodevelopment: Lower IQ scores are reported in formulated children compared with
  • breast fed children
  •  SIDS(Sudden Infant Death Syndrome): Formula feeding is associated with a higher
  • risk of infant mortality compared with breast feeding
  •  Infant Mortality : Formula feeding is associated with an increased risk of infant
  • mortality compared with breast feeding
  •  Asthma:There is a 1.7 fold risk of developing asthma among formula fed children with a
  • positive family history of asthma and a 1.4 fold risk of developing asthma among
  • formula fed children without a family history,compared with those who were breast fed
  • for 3 months or more
  •  Atopic Dermatitis : Infants with a family history of atopy who were exclusively
  • breastfed for less than 3 months have a 1.7 fold risk of atopic dermatitis compared with
  • infants who were exclusively breastfed.
  •  Type 1 Dermatitis : Less than 3 months of breast feeding has been associated with a 1.2
  • to 1.4 fold increased risk of developing type 1 diabetes compared with more than 3
  • months of breast feeding.
  •  Childhood Cancer:Several studies have examined associations between formula feeding
  • and childhood leukemia based on the hypothesis that immunoreactive factors in breast
  • milk may prevent viral infections implicated in the leukemia pathogenesis. (1 mark for
  • each point)
